uncited: It serves as the geometric anchor for [View Matrix Construction](1644-view-matrix-construction.md) when a global coordinate system is required.
The method aggregates translation and rotation components from a collection of poses.
Two distinct approaches exist in the literature: a vector-averaging approach and an SVD-based rotation averaging approach.
Format is either $[N, 3, 4]$ (rotation $3\times3$ + translation $3\times1$) or $[N, 4, 4]$ (homogeneous).
- Indices `[:, :3, 3]` denote the translation vectors (origins).
- Indices `[:, :3, 2]` denote the viewing direction vectors (z-axis).
- Indices `[:, :3, 1]` denote the up vectors (y-axis).
- Indices `[:, :3, :3]` denote the rotation matrices.
This method averages the position, viewing direction, and up vector directly.
**Compute Average Position**: Calculate the centroid of the camera origins.
where $\mathbf{t}_i$ is the translation vector of the $i$-th pose.
**Compute Average Viewing Direction**: Sum the z-axis vectors and normalize the result.
where $\mathbf{z}_i$ is the third column of the rotation matrix of the $i$-th pose.
**Compute Average Up Vector**: Sum the up vectors and normalize the result.
where $\mathbf{u}_i$ is the second column of the rotation matrix of the $i$-th pose.
This method ensures the resulting rotation matrix is orthogonal by applying Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to the mean rotation matrix.
where $\mathbf{R}_i$ is the $3\times3$ rotation submatrix of the $i$-th pose.
This step projects the mean rotation onto the Special Orthogonal group $SO(3)$.
- **Degenerate Configurations**: If all camera origins are identical, the average position is trivial.
If all viewing directions are identical, the z-axis is well-defined.
A guard should check for zero-norm vectors before normalization.
- **Memory Complexity**: $O(N)$ to store the input poses.
The output is constant size $O(1)$ (a single $4\times4$ matrix).
- **When to Use**: When a single reference frame is needed for rendering or alignment.
